The idea behind a basic income is essentially this: everyone in your neighborhood gets 3 grapes. One day, your neighbor finishes his residency, and you begin to see him bringing home pineapples, steak, and all sorts of shit that makes the grapes sour in your mouth. Now sure, lazy Larry across the street will moan and gripe but he'll keep eating the grapes. What about you? If you saw your neighbor eating grapes the same as you only to better his life and get all the foods you've ever dreamed of, will you be content wasting 10 hours a day in front of the TV? OR will you see what you can do to scrounge up something better?

The reason the idea came into being in the first place was to give the huge majority of Americans who spend every waking hour of their days struggling to meet their basic needs freedom from the struggle to survive.

At face value, it seems incredibly stupid (I once thought so as well), but ask yourself this question: if you weren't struggling to make ends meet, would you pursue your dreams?

We live in a society where we have the wealth to easily support everyone while keeping those at the top richer than God, and we are fast approaching a future where machines can do the work necessary to feed our species. Would our species be more productive answering telephones 14 hrs a day or letting each person intelligently pursue whatever they want?
